name: SPEC-02 typed-plaintext vectors, version 1
source: SPEC-02 sections 6.1, 6.2 and 6.7 (V1 to V26); X-vectors add the cases of T-9 and further rules of sections 6.1 and 6.2
notes: Every implementation of SPEC-02 sections 6.1 and 6.2 (the TypeScript classifier and reader, and the accord-core reference) MUST give these results.
class: control, envelope or legacy_text, decided from the leading bytes before any parsing (section 6.1).
envelope result: valid (rules 1 to 6 hold; attachments counts descriptors, unusable counts those that fail section 6.2.2), invalid (shown as "invalid message format"), or newer_version.

reason is informative and names the first rule that fails in the order: size, utf8, syntax/duplicate/surrogate/number/depth (as the parser meets them), version, shape; for control payloads: framing (no second 0x1E within 33 bytes), tag (syntax), unregistered (tag), size, utf8, the parse rules, shape (a single object with a string type and an integer v), unregistered (type or v).

accepted_by lists the consumer paths of REQ-53 that act on the plaintext (display, voice, key_distribution, control_queue). The display path acts on every content envelope, showing placeholders for invalid and newer ones. Legacy key JSON is accepted by the key-distribution path of clients that do not implement SPEC-05.
C is "7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7" and D the descriptor of section 6.2.3, both serialized without whitespace.

legacy_key_json marks legacy text that parses as an object whose type is skdm or nmk. Parses means: the text (invalid UTF-8 replaced by U+FFFD) passes rules 1, 2 and 4 of section 6.2 (depth at most 8), with any RFC 8259 number token allowed in place of rule 3. Neither JSON.parse nor serde_json is used, because they disagree on lone surrogates, out-of-range numbers and deep nesting (X57 to X65).

vectors.description: Body of 8,146 double quotes: 16,385 bytes in total
Line feed and two spaces, then V1
Duplicate type in a control payload
padded_size whose blob length exceeds CLIENT_MAX_BLOB_BYTES
Escaped high surrogate then a non-surrogate escape
Descriptor element that is not an object
One usable and one unusable descriptor
REQ-10 escape of user text that looks like an envelope
Control body that is an array
Legacy key JSON (untagged nmk) with leading whitespace
Legacy key JSON with an escaped lone surrogate: rule 2 holds for legacy key JSON, so this is displayed text (JSON.parse would accept it, serde_json would not)
Legacy key JSON with a number outside the f64 range: any RFC 8259 number token is allowed (JSON.parse would accept it, serde_json would not)
Legacy key JSON nested 129 levels deep: rule 4 holds with depth at most 8 (JSON.parse would accept it, serde_json would not)
Legacy key JSON nested 8 levels deep (the limit)
Legacy key JSON nested 9 levels deep
Legacy key JSON with fraction, exponent and negative number tokens
Legacy key JSON with a duplicate member: rule 1 holds for legacy key JSON
Legacy key JSON with a number token outside RFC 8259 (leading zero)
Legacy key JSON with a surrogate pair escape
